[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1524-1535)#### pub fn [try_replace_all_with](https://docs.rs#method.try_replace_all_with)<F>(
    &self,
    haystack: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    dst: &mut [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    replace_with: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [MatchError](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1524-1535)

#### pub fn [try_replace_all_with](https://docs.rs#method.try_replace_all_with)<F>(
    &self,
    haystack: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    dst: &mut [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    replace_with: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [MatchError](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchError.html)>

Replace all matches using a closure called on each match.
Matches correspond to the same matches as reported by
[ AhoCorasick::try_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.try_find_iter).

The closure accepts three parameters: the match found, the text of
the match and a string buffer with which to write the replaced text
(if any). If the closure returns `true`, then it continues to the next
match. If the closure returns `false`, then searching is stopped.

Note that any matches with boundaries that don’t fall on a valid UTF-8 boundary are silently skipped.

This is the fallible version of [ AhoCorasick::replace_all_with](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.replace_all_with).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-6)Errors

This returns an error when this Aho-Corasick searcher does not support
the default `Input` configuration. More specifically, this occurs only
when the Aho-Corasick searcher does not support unanchored searches
since this replacement routine always does an unanchored search.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

Basic usage:

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, MatchKind};
let patterns = &["append", "appendage", "app"];
let haystack = "append the app to the appendage";
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .match_kind(MatchKind::LeftmostFirst)
    .build(patterns)
    .unwrap();
let mut result = String::new();
ac.try_replace_all_with(haystack, &mut result, |mat, _, dst| {
    dst.push_str(&mat.pattern().as_usize().to_string());
    true
})?;
assert_eq!("0 the 2 to the 0age", result);
```
Stopping the replacement by returning `false` (continued from the
example above):

```
let mut result = String::new();
ac.try_replace_all_with(haystack, &mut result, |mat, _, dst| {
    dst.push_str(&mat.pattern().as_usize().to_string());
    mat.pattern() != PatternID::must(2)
})?;
assert_eq!("0 the 2 to the appendage", result);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1600-1611)

#### pub fn [try_replace_all_with_bytes](https://docs.rs#method.try_replace_all_with_bytes)<F>(

Replace all matches using raw bytes with a closure called on each
match. Matches correspond to the same matches as reported by
[ AhoCorasick::try_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.try_find_iter).

The closure accepts three parameters: the match found, the text of

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-7)Errors

the default `Input` configuration. More specifically, this occurs only
when the Aho-Corasick searcher does not support unanchored searches
since this replacement routine always does an unanchored search.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

Basic usage:

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, MatchKind};
let patterns = &["append", "appendage", "app"];
let haystack = b"append the app to the appendage";
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .match_kind(MatchKind::LeftmostFirst)

    .unwrap();

Stopping the replacement by returning `false` (continued from the

    dst.extend(mat.pattern().as_usize().to_string().bytes());

assert_eq!(b"0 the 2 to the appendage".to_vec(), result);

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1677-1683)#### pub fn [try_stream_find_iter](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_find_iter)<'a, R: [Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)>(
    &'a self,
    rdr: R,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[StreamFindIter](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamFindIter.html)<'a, R>, [MatchError](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchError.html)>

**crate feature **`std` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1677-1683)

#### pub fn [try_stream_find_iter](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_find_iter)<'a, R: [Read](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/trait.Read.html)>(
    &'a self,
    rdr: R,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[StreamFindIter](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamFindIter.html)<'a, R>, [MatchError](https://docs.rs/struct.MatchError.html)>

**crate feature**only.

`std`Returns an iterator of non-overlapping matches in the given
stream. Matches correspond to the same matches as reported by
[ AhoCorasick::try_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.try_find_iter).

The matches yielded by this iterator use absolute position offsets in
the stream given, where the first byte has index `0`. Matches are
yieled until the stream is exhausted.

Each item yielded by the iterator is an `Result<Match, std::io::Error>`, where an error is yielded if there was a problem
reading from the reader given.

When searching a stream, an internal buffer is used. Therefore, callers should avoiding providing a buffered reader, if possible.

This is the fallible version of [ AhoCorasick::stream_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.stream_find_iter).
Note that both methods return iterators that produce

`Result` values.
The difference is that this routine returns an error if *construction*of the iterator failed. The

`Result` values yield by the iterator
come from whether the given reader returns an error or not during the
search.[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-1)Memory usage

In general, searching streams will use a constant amount of memory for its internal buffer. The one requirement is that the internal buffer must be at least the size of the longest possible match. In most use cases, the default buffer size will be much larger than any individual match.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-8)Errors

This returns an error when this Aho-Corasick searcher does not support
the default `Input` configuration. More specifically, this occurs only
when the Aho-Corasick searcher does not support unanchored searches
since this stream searching routine always does an unanchored search.

This also returns an error if the searcher does not support stream
searches. Only searchers built with [ MatchKind::Standard](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html#variant.Standard) semantics
support stream searches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-basic-usage-8)Example: basic usage

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, PatternID};
let patterns = &["append", "appendage", "app"];
let haystack = "append the app to the appendage";
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(patterns).unwrap();
let mut matches = vec![];
for result in ac.try_stream_find_iter(haystack.as_bytes())? {
    let mat = result?;
    matches.push(mat.pattern());
}
assert_eq!(vec![
    PatternID::must(2),
    PatternID::must(2),
    PatternID::must(2),
], matches);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1751-1765)#### pub fn [try_stream_replace_all](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_replace_all)<R, W, B>(
    &self,
    rdr: R,
    wtr: W,
    replace_with: &[[B]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

**crate feature **`std` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1751-1765)

#### pub fn [try_stream_replace_all](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_replace_all)<R, W, B>(
    &self,
    rdr: R,
    wtr: W,
    replace_with: &[[B]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

**crate feature**only.

`std`Search for and replace all matches of this automaton in
the given reader, and write the replacements to the given
writer. Matches correspond to the same matches as reported by
[ AhoCorasick::try_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.try_find_iter).

Replacements are determined by the index of the matching pattern. For
example, if the pattern with index `2` is found, then it is replaced by
`replace_with[2]`.

After all matches are replaced, the writer is *not* flushed.

If there was a problem reading from the given reader or writing to the
given writer, then the corresponding `io::Error` is returned and all
replacement is stopped.

When searching a stream, an internal buffer is used. Therefore, callers should avoiding providing a buffered reader, if possible. However, callers may want to provide a buffered writer.

Note that there is currently no infallible version of this routine.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-2)Memory usage

In general, searching streams will use a constant amount of memory for its internal buffer. The one requirement is that the internal buffer must be at least the size of the longest possible match. In most use cases, the default buffer size will be much larger than any individual match.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-11)Panics

This panics when `replace_with.len()` does not equal
[ AhoCorasick::patterns_len](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.patterns_len).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-9)Errors

This returns an error when this Aho-Corasick searcher does not support
the default `Input` configuration. More specifically, this occurs only
when the Aho-Corasick searcher does not support unanchored searches
since this stream searching routine always does an unanchored search.

This also returns an error if the searcher does not support stream
searches. Only searchers built with [ MatchKind::Standard](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html#variant.Standard) semantics
support stream searches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-basic-usage-9)Example: basic usage

```
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let patterns = &["fox", "brown", "quick"];
let haystack = "The quick brown fox.";
let replace_with = &["sloth", "grey", "slow"];
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(patterns).unwrap();
let mut result = vec![];
ac.try_stream_replace_all(
    haystack.as_bytes(),
    &mut result,
    replace_with,
)?;
assert_eq!(b"The slow grey sloth.".to_vec(), result);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1829-1843)#### pub fn [try_stream_replace_all_with](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_replace_all_with)<R, W, F>(
    &self,
    rdr: R,
    wtr: W,
    replace_with: F,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html)>

**crate feature **`std` only.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1829-1843)

#### pub fn [try_stream_replace_all_with](https://docs.rs#method.try_stream_replace_all_with)<R, W, F>(
    &self,
    rdr: R,
    wtr: W,
    replace_with: F,

**crate feature**only.

`std`Search the given reader and replace all matches of this automaton
using the given closure. The result is written to the given
writer. Matches correspond to the same matches as reported by
[ AhoCorasick::try_find_iter](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html#method.try_find_iter).

The closure accepts three parameters: the match found, the text of the match and the writer with which to write the replaced text (if any).

After all matches are replaced, the writer is *not* flushed.

If there was a problem reading from the given reader or writing to the
given writer, then the corresponding `io::Error` is returned and all
replacement is stopped.

When searching a stream, an internal buffer is used. Therefore, callers should avoiding providing a buffered reader, if possible. However, callers may want to provide a buffered writer.

Note that there is currently no infallible version of this routine.

[§](https://docs.rs#memory-usage-3)Memory usage

In general, searching streams will use a constant amount of memory for its internal buffer. The one requirement is that the internal buffer must be at least the size of the longest possible match. In most use cases, the default buffer size will be much larger than any individual match.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-10)Errors

This returns an error when this Aho-Corasick searcher does not support
the default `Input` configuration. More specifically, this occurs only
when the Aho-Corasick searcher does not support unanchored searches
since this stream searching routine always does an unanchored search.

This also returns an error if the searcher does not support stream
searches. Only searchers built with [ MatchKind::Standard](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html#variant.Standard) semantics
support stream searches.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-basic-usage-10)Example: basic usage

```
use std::io::Write;
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let patterns = &["fox", "brown", "quick"];
let haystack = "The quick brown fox.";
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(patterns).unwrap();
let mut result = vec![];
ac.try_stream_replace_all_with(
    haystack.as_bytes(),
    &mut result,
    |mat, _, wtr| {
        wtr.write_all(mat.pattern().as_usize().to_string().as_bytes())
    },
)?;
assert_eq!(b"The 2 1 0.".to_vec(), result);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1847-2024)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-AhoCorasick-3)### impl [AhoCorasick](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html)

Routines for querying information about the Aho-Corasick automaton.

### impl [AhoCorasick](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasick.html)

Routines for querying information about the Aho-Corasick automaton.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1867-1869)#### pub fn [kind](https://docs.rs#method.kind)(&self) -> [AhoCorasickKind](https://docs.rs/enum.AhoCorasickKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1867-1869)

#### pub fn [kind](https://docs.rs#method.kind)(&self) -> [AhoCorasickKind](https://docs.rs/enum.AhoCorasickKind.html)

Returns the kind of the Aho-Corasick automaton used by this searcher.

Knowing the Aho-Corasick kind is principally useful for diagnostic
purposes. In particular, if no specific kind was given to
[ AhoCorasickBuilder::kind](https://docs.rs/struct.AhoCorasickBuilder.html#method.kind), then one is automatically chosen and
this routine will report which one.

Note that the heuristics used for choosing which `AhoCorasickKind`
may be changed in a semver compatible release.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, AhoCorasickKind};
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
// The specific Aho-Corasick kind chosen is not guaranteed!
assert_eq!(AhoCorasickKind::DFA, ac.kind());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1882-1884)#### pub fn [start_kind](https://docs.rs#method.start_kind)(&self) -> [StartKind](https://docs.rs/enum.StartKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1882-1884)

#### pub fn [start_kind](https://docs.rs#method.start_kind)(&self) -> [StartKind](https://docs.rs/enum.StartKind.html)

Returns the type of starting search configuration supported by this Aho-Corasick automaton.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, StartKind};
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(StartKind::Unanchored, ac.start_kind());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1901-1903)#### pub fn [match_kind](https://docs.rs#method.match_kind)(&self) -> [MatchKind](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1901-1903)

#### pub fn [match_kind](https://docs.rs#method.match_kind)(&self) -> [MatchKind](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html)

Returns the match kind used by this automaton.

The match kind is important because it determines what kinds of
matches are returned. Also, some operations (such as overlapping
search and stream searching) are only supported when using the
[ MatchKind::Standard](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html#variant.Standard) match kind.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, MatchKind};
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(MatchKind::Standard, ac.match_kind());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1927-1929)#### pub fn [min_pattern_len](https://docs.rs#method.min_pattern_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1927-1929)

#### pub fn [min_pattern_len](https://docs.rs#method.min_pattern_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Returns the length of the shortest pattern matched by this automaton.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

Basic usage:

```
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(3, ac.min_pattern_len());
```
Note that an `AhoCorasick` automaton has a minimum length of `0` if
and only if it can match the empty string:

```
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(0, ac.min_pattern_len());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1943-1945)#### pub fn [max_pattern_len](https://docs.rs#method.max_pattern_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1943-1945)

#### pub fn [max_pattern_len](https://docs.rs#method.max_pattern_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Returns the length of the longest pattern matched by this automaton.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

Basic usage:

```
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "quux", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(4, ac.max_pattern_len());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1965-1967)#### pub fn [patterns_len](https://docs.rs#method.patterns_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#1965-1967)

#### pub fn [patterns_len](https://docs.rs#method.patterns_len)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Return the total number of patterns matched by this automaton.

This includes patterns that may never participate in a match. For
example, if [ MatchKind::LeftmostFirst](https://docs.rs/enum.MatchKind.html#variant.LeftmostFirst) match semantics are used, and
the patterns

`Sam` and `Samwise` were used to build the automaton (in
that order), then `Samwise` can never participate in a match because
`Sam` will always take priority.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

Basic usage:

```
use aho_corasick::AhoCorasick;
let ac = AhoCorasick::new(&["foo", "bar", "baz"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(3, ac.patterns_len());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#2021-2023)#### pub fn [memory_usage](https://docs.rs#method.memory_usage)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/aho_corasick/ahocorasick.rs.html#2021-2023)

#### pub fn [memory_usage](https://docs.rs#method.memory_usage)(&self) -> [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)

Returns the approximate total amount of heap used by this automaton, in units of bytes.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

This example shows the difference in heap usage between a few configurations:

```
use aho_corasick::{AhoCorasick, AhoCorasickKind, MatchKind};
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .kind(None) // default
    .build(&["foobar", "bruce", "triskaidekaphobia", "springsteen"])
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(5_632, ac.memory_usage());
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .kind(None) // default
    .ascii_case_insensitive(true)
    .build(&["foobar", "bruce", "triskaidekaphobia", "springsteen"])
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(11_136, ac.memory_usage());
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .kind(Some(AhoCorasickKind::NoncontiguousNFA))
    .ascii_case_insensitive(true)
    .build(&["foobar", "bruce", "triskaidekaphobia", "springsteen"])
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(10_879, ac.memory_usage());
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .kind(Some(AhoCorasickKind::ContiguousNFA))
    .ascii_case_insensitive(true)
    .build(&["foobar", "bruce", "triskaidekaphobia", "springsteen"])
    .unwrap();
assert_eq!(2_584, ac.memory_usage());
let ac = AhoCorasick::builder()
    .kind(Some(AhoCorasickKind::DFA))
    .ascii_case_insensitive(true)
    .build(&["foobar", "bruce", "triskaidekaphobia", "springsteen"])
    .unwrap();
// While this shows the DFA being the biggest here by a small margin,
// don't let the difference fool you. With such a small number of
// patterns, the difference is small, but a bigger number of patterns
// will reveal that the rate of growth of the DFA is far bigger than
// the NFAs above. For a large number of patterns, it is easy for the
// DFA to take an order of magnitude more heap space (or more!).
assert_eq!(11_136, ac.memory_usage());
```
